title: Inside an Rc
subtitle: Clone, downgrade, upgrade and drop: watch the counters

captions.start: Rc::new allocates one block on the heap holding two counters and the value. a is the only strong owner.
captions.clone: Rc::clone copies the pointer into {v} and increments the strong count. The vector itself is not copied.
captions.downgrade: Rc::downgrade gives {v} a Weak: the weak count goes up, but a weak pointer does not keep the value alive.
captions.upgradeOk: upgrade() returned Some(Rc): the value is still alive, so {v} becomes a new strong owner. The Weak it came from still exists.
captions.upgradeNone: upgrade() returned None: there is no strong owner left and the value is already gone. This is how Weak breaks cycles safely.
captions.dropStrong: Dropping {v} decrements the strong count. The remaining owners keep the value alive.
captions.dropLast: {v} was the last strong owner: the value is dropped right now (its Drop runs and the Vec frees its buffer). The block stays allocated because weak pointers still point at the counters.
captions.dropWeak: Dropping the Weak in {v} decrements the weak count. It never affects the value itself.
captions.freedAfterWeak: The last Weak is gone too: both counters are zero, so the block itself is deallocated. Press Reset to start again.
captions.freedAll: {v} was the last owner and there are no weak pointers: the value is dropped and the block is deallocated in one go. Press Reset to start again.
